A later rebuild of the same source produced 5a9b4d08e619a995343761d29bb9d8e125a6cadb5de00b38ce9a76b35b9efa1e, so this incremental debug build is not byte-reproducible; the measured artifact is preserved at the path above and every result in this receipt refers to that hash.

crash.symptom: Windows fail-fast 0xc0000409 while entering rwkv_optimizer::tests::loss_unscale_and_adamw_share_one_command_stream in suite order
crash.root_cause: DeviceInner.pending_clears held PendingClear { buffer: GpuBuffer } strongly, so DeviceInner -> GpuBufferAllocation -> DeviceInner formed a reference cycle. Every zeroed intermediate dropped without being bound pinned its logical Vulkan device, and the suite exhausted driver resources. The named RWKV test was the victim of the exhaustion, not its cause.
fix: PendingClear stores Weak<GpuBufferAllocation>; an unreachable fill disappears with its last user.
An unbound fill whose allocation has no other owner is pruned at drain time (pending_clear_is_reachable), keeping the list bounded.

retirement_profile.correction: Phase IV reported 243.20 retirements/step and 142.107 ms/step for submit_and_restart. That divided a five-case run total by one case's step count, which is internally impossible next to the same step's 151 native submissions. The corrected per-case-step values are 48.64 and 28.42 ms; the readback site scales the same way (36.0 -> 7.20, 39.446 -> 7.89 ms).
retirement_profile.interpretation: 97.3% of the retirement cost is the fence/timeline wait for GPU work the following stage consumes. Host command-buffer rebuild is 0.329 ms per case-step (1.2%), so host-side coalescing cannot move step latency; only a dependency-level submission change could, and the previously measured streamed-wait intervals produced no gain.
